# proxmox_ha_rule (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox VE 9 high-availability placement rule through `/cluster/ha/rules`. Rules constrain how Proxmox HA places already HA-enrolled guests; they never start, stop, migrate, or wait for a guest. Each `resources` entry must reference a guest that is already HA configured, which the provider expresses by referencing `proxmox_ha_resource.<name>.resource_id`. Destroy removes only the rule.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

# Rules constrain guests that are already HA configured, so they reference
# proxmox_ha_resource. Provider credentials need Sys.Audit and Sys.Console on /.

# Keep the web guests on the fast nodes, with a relative priority.
resource "proxmox_ha_rule" "web_on_fast_nodes" {
  rule      = "web-fast-nodes"
  type      = "node-affinity"
  resources = [proxmox_ha_resource.web.resource_id]
  nodes = {
    node1 = 2
    node2 = 1
  }
  comment = "Prefer the fast nodes for web guests"
}

# Keep the primary and standby database guests apart. A negative rule needs at
# least as many cluster nodes as resources and pve-ha-manager 5.2.5 or later.
resource "proxmox_ha_rule" "database_apart" {
  rule      = "database-apart"
  type      = "resource-affinity"
  resources = [proxmox_ha_resource.database_primary.resource_id, proxmox_ha_resource.database_standby.resource_id]
  affinity  = "negative"
}

# Negative node affinity avoids the listed nodes instead of enumerating the
# allowed ones. Node priorities must stay 0. Disabled rules are still stored but
# no longer constrain scheduling.
resource "proxmox_ha_rule" "batch_off_backup_node" {
  rule      = "batch-off-backup"
  type      = "node-affinity"
  resources = [proxmox_ha_resource.batch.resource_id]
  nodes     = { backup1 = 0 }
  affinity  = "negative"
  strict    = true
  disable   = true
  comment   = "Keep batch guests off the backup node"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `resources` (Set of String) Canonical HA resource identifiers (`vm:<vmid>` or `ct:<vmid>`) the rule applies to. Proxmox requires at least one HA-configured resource, and at least two for `resource-affinity`.
- `rule` (String) HA rule identifier. Must start with a letter and may contain letters, numbers, `-`, and `_`. Changes require replacement.
- `type` (String) Rule type: `node-affinity` or `resource-affinity`. The type of an existing rule cannot change, so this requires replacement.

### Optional

- `affinity` (String) `positive` (prefer the given nodes / keep resources together) or `negative` (avoid the given nodes / keep resources apart). Required for `resource-affinity`; for `node-affinity` Proxmox defaults to `positive`, and `negative` needs `pve-ha-manager` 5.2.5 or later.
- `comment` (String) HA rule description.
- `disable` (Boolean) Keep the rule configured but exclude it from scheduling and feasibility checks. The Proxmox default is `false`.
- `nodes` (Map of Number) Cluster node names mapped to a relative priority, higher being more preferred. Required for `node-affinity` and not allowed for `resource-affinity`. With `affinity = "negative"` every priority must stay `0`.
- `strict` (Boolean) Whether `node-affinity` is strict: a strict rule restricts the resources to the given nodes instead of merely preferring them. Not allowed for `resource-affinity`. The Proxmox default is `false`.

### Read-Only

- `feasibility_errors` (Map of String) Feasibility errors Proxmox currently reports for this rule, keyed by the offending property (`resources`, `nodes`). Proxmox only checks the rule that is being written, so other rules can become infeasible without any Terraform change; infeasible rules are dropped by the scheduler and do nothing.
- `id` (String) HA rule identifier (same as `rule`).
- `order` (Number) Server-assigned evaluation ordinal of the rule.
